Asset: WELL-0043 (SW-23 Well 043, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: rod string Work started: 05 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 23 Nov 2022 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 427 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0043-0003 on 2022-11-03 Report written: 23 Nov 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0043-0003 showed the wellhead at 20.4 °C with the air at 17.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 16 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.

  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0043-029

Asset: WELL-0043 (SW-23 Well 043, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 01 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 04 May 2026 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 85 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0043-0179 on 2026-04-30 Report written: 05 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0043-0179 showed the wellhead at 30.6 °C with the air at 27.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 261 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 209 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0043-029 (WS-06).
